tools.name: get_plans
tools.description: Returns the plans of MyDataHub by Emailmovers, the UK B2B count engine: credit packs, credit rules, licence terms, the bounce warranty and the free trial, in GBP excluding VAT. Use it when the user asks what a list costs or which plan fits; it is free and needs no account. One credit buys one comple

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Returns the organisation's credit balance by source, plan, per-action prices and rate limit, and for an agent key its monthly budget and per-order cap. Use it before quoting a large order, or when a spend is refused, to see what remains. Free; it needs a token with account:read. Top-ups happen on my

tools.name: list_filters
tools.description: Lists every filterable field of the audience definition (mydatahub.audience/1) with its group, type, operators, value count and default, plus the datasets. Use it first to learn field names such as company.employee_band or site.town before building an audience by hand. Free and needs no account; the

tools.name: search_filter_values
tools.description: Searches the values of one field by text, such as towns matching leeds, and returns each code with its contact and company counts plus did_you_mean for near misses. Use the returned code in a filter rather than guessing one. Free and needs no account; results are paged with next_cursor. Call count_a

tools.name: expand_job_titles
tools.description: Expands title keywords into every matching title (plurals, department synonyms, ampersands, abbreviations such as CEO), each with a count, or shows what a bundle such as sdm resolves to. Use it before counting so the user can see and edit which titles a keyword covers; nothing is expanded silently.

tools.name: resolve_location
tools.description: Turns free text such as 20 miles of Leeds, Yorkshire or LS1 into region, county, town, postcode or radius filters, each with a count and a ready filter. Ambiguous places come back as candidates with a question, so ask the user which they meant rather than choosing. Free and needs no account, though

tools.name: compile_audience
tools.description: Compiles a plain English brief, such as 300 finance directors at law firms in Manchester, into an audience definition with a one-sentence readback, editable chips and any questions to answer first. Use it first for a request in words, read the readback to the user and settle the questions before cou

tools.name: count_audience
tools.description: Counts UK contacts and companies matching an audience, inline or a saved aud_ id, and returns Total, New to you and Emailable, up to three breakdowns, quality, the compliance summary, a price estimate and a count id. Use it whenever a filter changes, and before preview_records or quote_order, which

tools.name: preview_records
tools.description: Returns up to 25 masked sample rows (10 by default) for an audience or a count id, each with verification badges, why it matches and a provenance card. Use it after count_audience to show the user what the records look like before quoting. Free: emails and phones are masked on the server, a repeat r

tools.name: save_audience
tools.description: Saves an audience definition under a name, shared across the organisation, or updates a saved one when audience_id is given. Use it when the user wants to keep, share or recount a list later; saving is free and needs audiences:write. Repeating the same call returns the same saved audience. Call list

tools.name: list_audiences
tools.description: Lists the organisation's saved audiences with their current counts and last refresh, newest first, optionally filtered by name. Use it to find an aud_ id to count, quote or share. Free; it needs audiences:read. Pass an aud_ id to count_audience for a fresh count. Lawful basis is UK GDPR Article 6(1)

tools.name: list_field_sets
tools.description: Lists the field sets an order can deliver, such as standard or standard_telephone, with their exact columns. Every field set costs 1 credit a record, with no telephone, download or API surcharge. Use it to pick the field_set for quote_order; it is free and needs no account. Lawful basis is UK GDPR A

tools.name: quote_order
tools.description: Creates a machine quote for a count: the records you would receive after removing ones already held and suppressed, the credits and GBP price, the licence, the warranty and any blockers. The quote_id lasts 24 hours and is bound to the dataset version; it is not a human sales quote, which is a 14 day

tools.name: create_order
tools.description: Spends 1 credit per complete UK record against a live machine quote from quote_order, and queues the order. It needs the quote_id and an idempotency_key to reuse on any retry, so a retry never charges twice; a flag set by a model is never consent. Where the host supports elicitation the user confirm

tools.name: get_order
tools.description: Returns one order's status (queued, building, verifying, ready, failed or cancelled), counts, charges, licence and links to its records, download and receipt, or the recent orders when order_id is left out. Use it after create_order to wait for ready, or rely on the order.ready webhook. Free; it nee

tools.name: fetch_order_records
tools.description: Returns a page of an order's delivered records (50 by default, up to 100) with the licence block on every page, as JSON or, on request, as CSV. Pages stay under about 8,000 tokens, with approx_tokens on each; pass next_cursor to continue. Fetching again under licence costs 0 credits; it needs record

tools.name: push_to_crm
tools.description: Pushes an order's records to a connected CRM such as HubSpot or Salesforce, keyed on mydatahub_record_id, as record operations only: nothing is ever sent to the contacts. dry_run defaults to true and reports what would be created, updated or skipped; a live push needs the user's confirmation or an a

tools.name: lookup_company
tools.description: Looks up one company by Companies House number, domain or name and returns its Companies House fields and compliance facts, and for a signed-in caller the contacts held there by job level. tools.name: enrich_contact
tools.description: Returns the full record for one known person, matched by email or by name with a company name, number or domain. tools.name: check_suppression
tools.description: Checks the suppression status of up to 1,000 delivered records by record id, as of now, and names the lists that suppress each. Use it before every send, because objections reach records after delivery. Free; it needs suppressions:read. Leave suppressed records out of the send, and call report_objec

tools.name: report_objection
tools.description: Records an objection to direct marketing for one record, by record id or email hash. Scope licensee suppresses it for your organisation at once; scope emailmovers suppresses it database-wide within one working day and tells every licensee holding it. Free; it needs suppressions:write, and repeating

tools.name: get_compliance_receipt
tools.description: Returns an order's signed compliance receipt: an ES256 JWS with its decoded claims and a PDF link, covering records delivered, suppression removals, subscriber classes, TPS screening, Article 14 status, the licence and the file hash. Use it to prove to the user, a colleague or another agent that a l
